Transformer-based recommenders can amplify popularity bias as they scale: increasing model depth improves accuracy but can cause spectral collapse that favors popular items over niche ones [1]. SPRINT mitigates this by constraining attention-score column sums and feed-forward parameter spectral norms, improving accuracy and long-tail fairness [1].

Other work addresses sequential or generative recommenders with different approaches: PR-entmax modifies the training objective without architectural changes [3], PopSteer steers popularity-related neuron activations post hoc [6], and BT-SR uses noncontrastive self-supervised learning to improve long-tail coverage [8].
